name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: Elon Musk vs. ActBlue
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
**$455 million.**
That is how much money Elon Musk has personally spent this year to help Republicans hold the House and the Senate. That number is not up to the second, so as you read this the total is likely higher.
Let me put that number in perspective for you.
**$275 million.**
That is how much money was donated to Democratic federal campaigns and committees across all of ActBlue during the month of September alone. That money was raised from more than 6 million individual donations giving an average of around $40 apiece.
Think about that.
In this country, we have conditioned ourselves to accept as normal that one man can have a greater financial impact than 6 million donations from regular folks who are acting to elect people they believe will prioritize their needs over the needs of people who already have it all.
And what does Elon Musk do it for?
A. As the richest man in the world, he does it for his own tax cuts and,
B. His billions of dollars for his own federal contracts.
And that is just one man. Nine of the top ten donors this cycle are Republicans according to the _Washington Post_. These numbers are as of more than a week ago.
* Elizabeth & Richard Uihlein: $138 million
* Jeff & Janine Yass: $110 million
* Ben Horowitz & Marc Andreessen: $92 million
* Miriam Adelson: $68 million
* Cameron & Tyler Winklevoss: $55 million
* Paul Singer: $54 million
* Greg & Anna Brockman: $50 million
* Christine & Stephen Schwarzman: $36 million
Do you think they give that money as an act of charity? I think we all know how this works. These mega-donors are giving that much money because they are expecting a return. It's an investment.
And the outcomes we get are not a surprise.
That is oligarchy.
From the start, I have funded my campaigns differently because I believe you cannot accept the same money that is used to oppress the working people of this country.
There are a lot of folks in races tougher than mine who say it's naive to swear off that corporate money.
I say it's what we need.
I say it's what you deserve.
You deserve a government that answers to you, not the people writing the checks.
You deserve a government that takes on corporate greed rather than takes their money.
Our average donation is $16.
I am very proud of that fact.
Because in the history of this country, great change has almost always come from the bottom-up. It happens when lots and lots of people are willing to stand up and say ENOUGH and to fight for what we believe in.
We may not raise as much as Elon Musk gives, but we do raise quite a bit ... and most importantly the way we do it tells me we are on the right track. That we are building the foundations of a movement with the ability to take on the greed of the billionaire class in this country.
And the truth is, the single greatest source of donations we receive comes in response to emails like this one. Which means if we are going to continue to fund our work, our organizers, our rallies, our donations to progressive candidates... it means from time-to-time I have to ask:
[ Can you please make a contribution to my campaign today? Our average donation is around $16. Some give more. Some give less. All that matters is that lots and lots of people are chipping-in and the rest will take care of itself. ](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261024-12473-P_FND_EXP_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12473%2E2526796%2EyamAY0)

Thank you for your continued support.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

That number is not up to the second, so as you read this the total is likely higher. Let me put that number in perspective for you. $275 million. That is how much money was donated to Democratic federal campaigns and committees across all of ActBlue during the month of September alone. That money was raised from more than 6 million individual donations giving an average of around $40 apiece. Think about that. In this country, we have conditioned ourselves to accept as normal that one man can have a greater financial impact than 6 million donations from regular folks who are acting to elect people they believe will prioritize their needs over the needs of people who already have it all. And what does Elon Musk do it for? A. As the richest man in the world, he does it for his own tax cuts and, B. His billions of dollars for his own federal contracts. And that is just one man. Nine of the top ten donors this cycle are Republicans according to the Washington Post. These numbers are as of more than a week ago. Elizabeth & Richard Uihlein: $138 million Jeff & Janine Yass: $110 million Ben Horowitz & Marc Andreessen: $92 million Miriam Adelson: $68 million Cameron & Tyler Winklevoss: $55 million Paul Singer: $54 million Greg & Anna Brockman: $50 million Christine & Stephen Schwarzman: $36 million Do you think they give that money as an act of charity? I think we all know how this works. These mega-donors are giving that much money because they are expecting a return. It's an investment. And the outcomes we get are not a surprise. That is oligarchy. From the start, I have funded my campaigns differently because I believe you cannot accept the same money that is used to oppress the working people of this country. There are a lot of folks in races tougher than mine who say it's naive to swear off that corporate money. I say it's what we need. I say it's what you deserve. You deserve a government that answers to you, not the people writing the checks. You deserve a government that takes on corporate greed rather than takes their money. Our average donation is $16. I am very proud of that fact. Because in the history of this country, great change has almost always come from the bottom-up. It happens when lots and lots of people are willing to stand up and say ENOUGH and to fight for what we believe in. We may not raise as much as Elon Musk gives, but we do raise quite a bit ... and most importantly the way we do it tells me we are on the right track. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Why we built the Mississippi Wire
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/whyismssoawesome-12855253?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
Who is reporting on your county board of supervisors? Your school board? Your city council? A generation ago, the answer was obvious. The local paper sent a reporter. He sat through the meeting, took notes, and you read about it over breakfast the next morning. Today, across much of Mississippi, the answer is no one. Local newspapers did not decline because people stopped caring about what happens in their town. They declined because Big Tech took the advertising that paid for the reporting. The classifieds went online. The display ads went to Google and Facebook. And the reporters who used to cover the courthouse were let go. That matters more than it might seem. Self-government depends on people knowing what their government is doing. Thomas Jefferson put it bluntly — offered a choice between government without newspapers or newspapers without government, he said he would not hesitate to prefer the latter. When no one is in the room, officials answer to no one. Decisions about your taxes, your schools, and your roads get made without anyone outside the building ever hearing about them. So we decided to do something about it. We built the Mississippi Wire. I have recorded a short video explaining why. In it, I set out how the local newspaper model broke down, what has been lost as a result — and how the Wire uses new technology to do the kind of reporting newspapers used to do, region by region, from the Delta to the Coast.

You can watch it [here](https://us.list-manage.com/bzUecpPdpwE?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3).
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/ft_x3czXFfo?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)
---
| The Wire is not about opinion. It is about telling Mississippians what their officials said and did - plainly, and in time for it to matter. Big Tech hollowed out local news. It turns out new technology can help bring it back. Please take a few minutes to watch the video, and then take a look at mississippiwire.news for yourself. Have a wonderful weekend!

You deserve an explanation.
In just a second, we are going to ask you to make your first donation to Eileen Laubacher’s campaign against Lauren Boebert in Colorado. Please give us a chance to explain why this request – especially during this moment – is so important.
Here is the truth: We have received an extraordinary number of donations from grassroots donors. Help from people like you is entirely how we fund this campaign. We don’t take money from corporate PACs. Eileen is proud of that fact, and you should be too.
But Lauren Boebert's Super PACs are absolutely hammering Eileen on TV with attack ads right now. And right now, we’re still behind in the polls.

body:
Dear Peter, Hot off the press! Yesterday, the _St. Albans Messenger_ endorsed Molly for Lieutenant Governor, and we wanted to share the good news and give you a little weekend reading. In his endorsement, Editor Emeritus Emerson Lynn made the case for why Molly is the right choice for Vermont: “In the lieutenant governor’s race between Republican John Rogers and Democrat Molly Gray, the candidate who best meets Vermont’s needs is Ms. Gray...For two basic reasons: first, she’s a strong communicator, and second, we need someone in the office who is willing and able to take on the Trump administration’s persistent attack on the country’s civil rights... Ms. Gray has the talent we need. She has the experience that will make her efficient in the job. She is the communicator who can bring us together to solve our challenges. And, most importantly, she has the integrity necessary to weave together Vermonters who need to know they are being told the truth. _New Mexicans are feeling the consequences of Donald Trump’s policies, and they need a Governor who will fight for them.
_

With just 10 days left, every bit of grassroots support matters. If you have a minute, let us explain exactly why that’s happening — and what you can do to help GIFFORDS fight back.
#

Team —
If you’ve spent any time watching TV lately, you know Democrats are getting absolutely pummeled. And if you have a minute, we hope you’ll let us explain exactly why that’s happening — and what you can do to help GIFFORDS fight back.
In the 2020 election, the NRA and their Super PAC spent about $42 million, down from more than $50 million in 2016. And in 2024? Just $10 million. If you can believe it, the NRA is on the run. That’s worth celebrating.
But here’s the problem: They’ve been replaced by something even bigger. In 2024, Elon Musk spent about $300 million supporting Donald Trump and the GOP. That’s not the NRA, and it isn’t even the entire gun lobby. It’s one person. It’s outrageous, and it’s getting worse.
Elon Musk has put $366 million into the 2026 election to help Donald Trump and the GOP hold their majority. Democrats are under relentless pressure right now, and we have to move fast to respond.
We know a donation of $5 or $10 doesn’t seem like all that much against Musk’s millions, but it isn’t just your donation. By the time you’ve read this far, dozens of others have chipped in. Now, they’re hoping you’ll do the same.

subject: I gave the green light
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Alex Vindman for Florida
body:
It was a tough choice
Peter, it’s Eugene Vindman. I just made the toughest decision I’ve had to this election cycle and need to share it with you.
Over the weekend, my opponent launched another attack ad against me. It’s an ad made entirely with AI, and it implies I am hurting working Virginians' paychecks. On top of that, he’s linking to a website he’s created, devoted entirely to slandering me.
My team and I came together to determine our response strategy, and our best option was to urgently expand our advertising and voter outreach efforts to compete with his ads, set the record straight, and get undecided voters on our side before Election Day.
That meant expanding our TV ad buys and putting more organizers on the ground. Those are pretty steep expenses, Peter. But with nearly two weeks until Election Day, I gave my team the green light.
Here’s the problem you need to know though:
It wasn’t an easy decision. Let me quickly explain:
**We don’t have the money in the budget to approve this expense. But I took the risk anyway because it’s what we need to do to win — and because I bet on this team, knowing you will help us fill the budget gap.**
That’s how much faith I have in this team and our fight to hold this seat, flip the House blue, and stop Donald Trump.
Peter, I know for a fact that we have two advantages in this race: our commitment to defending our democracy — and you.
We can't afford to leave voters unreached in a race this close. I'm counting on grassroots supporters like you to help fill the gap we've created by investing more in reaching voters before Election Day.
I hope you'll step up and join us in this fight.
So, on the heels of my difficult budget decision, I’m asking:

name: Darline Graham
subject: Breaking it down
body:
We have 10 days left. Let me explain what's at stake. |
---

Fellow Patriot -

Here's a breakdown of our race ... _by the numbers_.

**$9 million:**
This is how much Annie Andrews raised last quarter.
I got into this race long after she was already raising millions of dollars from liberals all over the country. She has the support of Hollywood stars like Star Wars' Mark Hamill and Roseanne's John Goodman.

**3 months:**
How long I've been in this race.
I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot. I never thought I'd be in this position. Politics was Lindsey's thing. But when President Trump asked me to run for a full Senate term, I knew I had to answer the call to, once again, serve the people of South Carolina.

Since entering, I am running my third statewide campaign in just three months. I know so many of you have been so generous to help me, but it's taken its toll. Our campaign is running on fumes.

**RCP Average: +2.7:**
**Darline Graham: 48%**
**Annie Andrews: 45.3%**
This is the average of all the recent polls in the South Carolina Senate races. We're only up by 2.7%.

Annie Andrews and her liberal Super PACs have spent millions attacking me, spreading lies about my family and me. She's also lying about where she stands on the issues. She's wearing a "moderate mask" that will disappear IF she's elected to the Senate to stand with Chuck Schumer, James Talarico, and Abdul El-Sayed.

body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
With just 10 days left until Election Day, I don’t have any time to waste
— and I’m sure you don’t either. So I’ll get right to the point:

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20087?t=1001&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]Derek, will you
please rush a $10 donation to my reelection campaign to help me defend
Pennsylvania from the far-right?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20087?t=1002&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]Rush $10 →

Look, I know what you’re thinking: A donation this late in the game isn’t
going to make any sort of impact in this race.

But Derek, that
couldn’t be more wrong. Let me tell you why:

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20087?t=1003&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]$10 plants one more yard sign in a neighborhood near
you.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20087?t=1004&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]$10 reaches one more voter who still hasn’t made up their mind in this
race.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20087?t=1005&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]$10 mobilizes one more supporter who forgot to submit their mail-in
ballot.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20087?t=1006&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]$10 launches one more ad that could reach hundreds, if not thousands,
of voters with our message.

In a swing state like Pennsylvania, every single vote matters — and so
does every single dollar. My team and I aren’t going to waste a single
second getting our message out to voters in the final days of this race —
and if you’re with me, then I have to ask:

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20087?t=1007&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]Can I count on you to rush $10 — one for every day left in our campaign
— to support this grassroots movement in the final sprint towards Election
Day?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20353?t=1008&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]Donate $10 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20354?t=1009&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]Donate $25 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20355?t=1010&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]Donate $50 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20356?t=1011&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]Donate $100 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20357?t=1012&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]Donate $250 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/20093?t=1013&akid=758%2E245147%2EGwMT3y ]Other →

Thank you,

Josh Shapiro

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with supporters like you.
